findings.evidence: template/scripts/execute_requirement.py:217 calls requirement_board.reconcile_nonterminal before any terminal check. requirement_board.py:20-24 maps stage 'done' to 'In progress', and lines 41-44 write whenever the current status differs. Earlier, the only reconcile was after a child start (line 286), so a Done card was never touched on a terminal rerun. The change does not show that this path is guarded.
findings.summary: The unconditional card reconcile at advance() entry can rewrite an already terminal (Done) Requirement card back to In progress if advance is rerun after delivery.

findings.evidence: tests/test_requirement_card_claim.py exercises only requirement_intake start. tests/test_requirement_execution.py only changes an expected call count to 2 and adds mock.patch.object(execution.requirement_board, 'reconcile_nonterminal') to two tests. The spec scenario 'a card still showing Ready is repaired to In progress at entry' has no direct test.
findings.summary: Nothing tests the new advance-entry claim itself: that it runs before slow steps, repairs a Ready card, or surfaces a reconcile failure.
